added: packages/local-companion (@sos-2/local-companion): the authenticated local companion contract — the LOCAL BODY PATH over the merged P5 Harness Contract. (1) Session/authentication: pairing + session records as typed records over INJECTED seams (PairingAuthority port — the companion cannot mint sessions or authority; CredentialStore port — session token VALUES go straight into the store and never echo/log/serialize, only NAMES, the P8 sandbox secrets discipline; ReferencePairingAuthority is a deterministic in-process fake with an injected code allowlist; session status ACTIVE/EXPIRED/REVOKED/UNPAIRED re-evaluated per access against the injected clock + token validation — never cached as truth). (2) Private workspace/file access is scope-granted: immutable CompanionScopeGrant records (roots with read/read-write modes, process allowlist, expiry) arrive from pairing; a granted-scope check runs before EVERY access (unknown root, absolute path, '..' escape, dot-segment, read-only-root write or an EXPIRED grant — grants are re-evaluated against the injected clock before consequential operations — answers a typed COMPANION_SCOPE_DENIED denial, never silent, never a crash); the access dispatches onto the injectable LocalFilePort (in-memory reference runtime). (3) Local shell/process integration: typed operation records through the injectable LocalProcess seam — the reference SimulatedLocalProcess is a deterministic in-process simulator with an injectable command registry (built-ins echo/cat/ls/pwd; ZERO real process spawning in library code); a command outside the granted process allowlist is a typed COMPANION_PROCESS_DENIED denial (an un-granted consequential operation never runs). (4) Offline queueing: LocalWorkOrder (the §9 step subset the companion body advertises + authority grant refs) + OfflineWorkQueue (FIFO, enqueue-total audit) — local-only work orders QUEUE while the device reports offline and run when it reconnects; cloud tasks never require the companion. (5) Reconnect + state reconciliation: the durable LocalEventLog (contiguous 1-based sequences, monotonic ingestion-acknowledgement watermark) reconciles against the merged P2 ObservationEventRepository through its idempotent, replay-protected ingestion (deterministic event ids local-companion:<device>:<event_id>) — exactly-once (APPLIED and DUPLICATE both prove the store holds the event; a lost-acknowledgement restart deduplicates exactly), gap-free sequence continuity (reconciliation PRE-SCANS the pending suffix and a gap aborts the whole pass with a typed COMPANION_RECONCILIATION_GAP violation before the store ingests anything). (6) Local observations are provenance-labelled: every LocalEventRecord carries [source, device:<device_id>, producer:local-companion@<version>] with a @sos-2/provenance Producer record (the @sos-2/telemetry provenance discipline) and the labels survive P2 ingestion verbatim. (7) LocalCompanionBody implements the merged P5 HarnessContract at placement user-device: honest advertisement (terminal + filesystem, shell exec, isolationLevel none, egress none, git/browser/runtimeIntegrations empty -> typed UNSUPPORTED — explicit, never silent), companion denials surface as truthful FAILED results carrying the typed codes, body observations land in the provenance-labelled local event log, cursor-based event stream, deterministic artifact ids, no authority fields anywhere on the surface (frozen P5 rule). (8) Honest installation statuses: COMPANION_INSTALLATION_STATUSES with the reference NOT_YET_INSTALLED + simulated marker (no real desktop app ships; evidence never fabricated; a simulated runtime claiming INSTALLED is rejected loudly).

packages/browser-bridge (@sos-2/browser-bridge): the OPTIONAL browser bridge — the §4 tier-4 ('extension') adapter contract bridging a browser extension onto the companion/harness surface. Typed ports with injectable transports (the P8 LocalBridgeTransport command-dispatch precedent): bridge.browser.open / bridge.browser.interact commands over an injectable BrowserBridgeTransport carrying the `simulated` honesty marker; the adapter serves the §9-shaped operations (BrowserOpenRequest/BrowserInteractRequest -> HarnessResult) reply-validated against exact typed shapes — a malformed reply is a truthful FAILED, never a silent success. THE SEAM CARRIES NO AUTHORITY: every marshaled request/reply is validated against an EXACT field set — a smuggled grant/permission/authority key (request-side OR reply-side) is a typed violation NAMING the field (browser extensions are adapters, never SOS authorities — pinned by tests in both directions). Honest connection statuses consumed from the merged P8 vocabulary: NOT_YET_CONNECTED while no real extension exists (null transport — connection evidence never fabricated), the explicit simulated marker when the deterministic SimulatedBrowserExtensionTransport (fixture page model, deterministic page-id sequences) backs the bridge. NO real browser extension ships; real extensions implement the transport with simulated: false later without contract change.

packages/ide-bridge (@sos-2/ide-bridge): the OPTIONAL IDE bridge — the SAME tier-4 adapter discipline for IDE integrations (the §1 'IDE or desktop interaction' body surface): bridge.ide.openFile / bridge.ide.diagnostics commands over an injectable IdeBridgeTransport; typed IdeDiagnostic records (severity/code/message/line); reply-validated exact shapes; the anti-smuggling rule names smuggled authority fields on both request and reply sides; honest NOT_YET_CONNECTED while no real IDE plugin exists with the explicit simulated marker for the deterministic SimulatedIdeIntegrationTransport (document-id sequences, fixture diagnostics). NO real IDE plugin ships; real plugins implement the transport later without contract change.

apps/companion (@sos-2/companion): the local companion host — a plain Node + TypeScript host (repo-standard ESM + tsc build, no vendor framework; the apps/api + apps/worker-runtimes precedent) whose composition root is the single impure boundary (SystemClock + index.ts). Commands (run-work-order / pair-companion / reconcile) + CommandSource (poll + non-destructive peek) + UserDevicePresence are INJECTED ports; the host runs on an injected tick source with a bounded drain (no ambient timers). The §7 user-device model is enforced at the scheduling gate: a work order whose requirements demand placement user-device QUEUES while the device reports offline (the local queue carries exactly the companion-body operation subset — a step outside it is refused loudly at enqueue, never silently dropped) and runs when it reconnects; cloud/remote orders run regardless and NEVER consult device presence (zero device probes — pinned by tests). The reconnect discipline: reconcile FIRST (exactly-once, gap-free), then release + run the queued orders FIFO. Released orders execute through the fabric's uniform gate pipeline (TASK -> LEASE -> AUTHORITY -> ADVERTISEMENT -> DISPATCH) with the §10 honest verification record (a denied/unsupported/failed step completes with verified:false — never fabricated). createReferenceCompanionRuntime assembles the durable in-memory P2 stores + broker + fabric + companion core + §9 companion body (registered at user-device) + queue + host + the tier-4 bridges behind simulated transports + the honest installation status; queued local work while offline is the STABLE §7 state (idle = no further progress possible without external change).

tests/local-bridges (@sos-2/local-bridge-contracts): the acceptance suites. Cloud-independence: a full cloud-body journey (the P8 cloud journey re-run) completes in a COMPANION-ABSENT world — the proof file imports ZERO P11 packages, pinned STRUCTURALLY by the structure scan reading its import specifiers (no companion object, bridge, queue, event log or device-presence port exists in that journey). Offline queueing: local-only work orders queue while the device is offline and run on reconnect — nothing lost or duplicated (exactly two durable task records, both COMPLETED verified, the private workspace content really written, queue fully drained with the audit total preserved); a cloud order through the SAME host runs with the device offline and ZERO device probes. Scope enforcement: out-of-scope roots, absolute paths, '..' escapes, read-only-root writes and un-granted process commands are typed denials inside truthful FAILED results through the PUBLIC §9 contract behind the P5 broker (per-reason assertions); an EXPIRED scope grant authorizes NOTHING (re-evaluated before consequential operations); denials are durable observations. Reconnect reconciliation: exactly-once with gap-free continuity; a lost-acknowledgement restart deduplicates exactly (the companion-event count never doubles); a gappy log aborts with the typed COMPANION_RECONCILIATION_GAP violation and NOTHING ingested (fail-closed). Provenance: every local event and every ingested observation name the local source + device identity + producer label, and SECRETS NEVER ECHO (output scans across session records, event logs, observation events, task records and bridge replies for the session-token prefix and out-of-scope private content); the whole journey is deterministic (fixed clock, re-run equality). Bridges are adapters: no authority fields marshal across any bridge (request + reply smuggling named per field), malformed replies are truthful FAILED, honest NOT_YET_CONNECTED/NOT_YET_INSTALLED surfaces never fabricate connection evidence, tier-4 rank alignment with the frozen §4 order. Structural scans: zero new external dependencies (workspace:* + the existing toolchain only, checked against the base lockfile), the existing workspace globs cover the new packages, offline determinism (no Date.now/Math.random/fetch/process.env/ambient timers/child_process in the owned sources outside the documented apps/companion composition boundary), the repository's fixed vitest seed, only merged + P11-owned workspace imports (unmerged siblings P6/P7 never referenced), no relative imports escaping an owned package, and the cloud-independence import discipline.
